text:
AcmeCorp-ops: Hey team — since 02:00 UTC our prod app (private VPC) started getting sporadic inference failures to Redwood. TLS errors and 523-style timeouts. Only from this VPC, public customers unaffected.

maria (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the client-side error and a short tcpdump or packet trace? Also which region and IPs you're hitting?

AcmeCorp-ops: Error seen in app logs: "TLS handshake failed: EOF during handshake". curl from a bastion in the same subnet sometimes works, sometimes gets "connection reset by peer". Hitting api.redwood-inference.us-east-1.internal (private endpoint via NAT).

kevin (Infra): Quick suspicion: stateful vs stateless firewall (NACL) + ephemeral return ports. If NACL is blocking high-ports inbound for return traffic you'll see RSTs after the handshake. Can you share your subnet NACL rules?

AcmeCorp-ops: NACL is locked down per security policy. Outbound rules allow 443 -> 0.0.0.0/0, inbound only allows 443 from our load balancer. We thought return traffic was covered.

jia (SRE): Heads-up: network ACLs are stateless — you must explicitly allow the ephemeral port range on both inbound and outbound. Typical ephemeral range is 1024-65535 (Linux/modern). If outbound to 443 succeeds but inbound ephemeral return ports are denied, the connection will not complete (SYN, SYN-ACK, then RST).

AcmeCorp-ops: That matches our tcpdump. Snippet: 

--- tcpdump 
12:02:10.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.49158 > api.redwood-inference.https: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0], length 0
12:02:10.124010 IP api.redwood-inference.https > 10.0.5.12.49158: Flags [S.], seq 1000, ack 1, win 28960, length 0
12:02:10.124200 IP 10.0.5.12.49158 > api.redwood-inference.https: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0

So we see an immediate R from our side after SYN-ACK — indicates our stack or a middlebox is killing the session.

maria (Support): Thanks. Two likely causes: (1) NACL dropping inbound ephemeral ports (stateless), (2) DPI / firewall performing TLS inspection or session termination (explicit RST) because SNI mismatch or cert pinning. Because curl sometimes works, sounds like intermittent inspection or per-flow hashing issue on the FW/NAT.

kevin (Infra): Steps to triage (quick):
- From bastion run: sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host <client-ip> and reproduce.
- Check NACL rules: aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc> (or UI). Confirm inbound rule for 1024-65535 allowing TCP from 0.0.0.0/0 and outbound same range to 0.0.0.0/0.
- Check NAT/GW/Firewall logs for SYN/FIN/RST decisions around the timestamps.

jia (SRE): If you can't open full ephemeral range, you can try narrower ranges used by your OS: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range shows e.g., "32768 60999". Allow that range both directions in the NACL. Also check conntrack table sizing: sudo conntrack -L | grep <client-ip> to see state.

AcmeCorp-ops: We checked conntrack: entries present but some sockets move to TIME_WAIT then connection resets. Firewall logs show "DPI: TLS_FAILED_SNI_MISMATCH" for a subset. We have an inline TLS inspection appliance that occasionally mangles the session when client uses TLS1.3 + 0-RTT.

maria (Support): Actionable repro & workaround:
1) Temporarily open ephemeral range on the subnet NACL (both inbound/outbound) for the test subnets.
2) Bypass DPI device (put path through non-inspecting route) or disable TLS inspection for *.redwood-inference.* hostnames.
3) If you need a minimal change: allow the exact local_port_range (sysctl) both ways in the NACL; that usually fixes RSTs.

kevin (Infra): Example NACL entries (order matters):
Inbound: rule 100 allow TCP 32768-60999 0.0.0.0/0 
Outbound: rule 100 allow TCP 32768-60999 0.0.0.0/0
Plus keep your existing 443 allow rules.

AcmeCorp-ops: Will try now. One question: can Redwood provide deterministic IPs for private endpoints so we can limit egress allowlist instead of 0.0.0.0/0?

maria (Support): We can provide the private endpoint IP range for your region — I'll DM you the CIDR list and resource IDs. For dedicated/private customers we also support a fixed egress set via peering config.

netbot: config-change-notification: rule update started by AcmeCorp-ops at 12:12 UTC.

AcmeCorp-ops: After opening 32768-60999 both in/out and bypassing DPI, errors stopped for 30m of load testing. Looks stable. Thanks! :tada:

jia (SRE): Follow-up recommendations:
- Make the NACL change permanent for the subnets that run inference clients, or better: rely on Security Groups + stateful NAT in front of hosts so you don't need broad NACLs.
- If you must keep DPI, whitelist redwood hostname or disable 0-RTT for inspected flows.
- Add a synthetic probe from that subnet to monitor TLS handshake variance.

maria (Support): I'll open a support ticket with the CIDR list and steps we walked through. Marking as resolved pending your post-change verification.

AcmeCorp-ops: Verified stable. Closing this thread. Thanks all.
